title: "About Me"

All previous drafts of this page were genuinely painful to write. I despise self-aggrandizment, but there's no good way to write "about me" without it. So rather than do that, I'll just live you with a series of thoughts, snippets, and quotes that I find meaningful. Hopefully it you something about me.

# Snippets

> [Andrew Gelman](https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2022/06/08/how-can-a-top-scientist-be-so-confidently-wrong-r-a-fisher-and-smoking-example/): Brilliance represents an upper bound on the quality of your reasoning, but there is no lower bound. The most brilliant scientist in the world can take really dumb stances. Indeed, the success that often goes with brilliance can encourage a blind stubbornness. Not always—some top scientists are admirably skeptical of their own ideas—but sometimes. And if you want to be stubborn, again, there’s no lower bound on how wrong you can be.
